name: Auckland Central
description: Auckland Central covers Auckland’s city centre, suburbs such as Ponsonby, Newton and Arch Hill, as well as the islands of the Hauraki Gulf. It is currently held by Green party co-leader Chlöe Swabrick, who won the electorate with a margin of 16,624 votes and has held the seat since 2020. National won the party vote in 2023 with 33%, followed by the Green Party on 24%. Barring one three year gap, the seat was held continuously by Labour from 1919-2008, but it has not regained it since.

name: Banks Peninsula
description: Banks Peninsula covers the area to the east and south of Christchurch, including Akaroa, Lyttleton, and southern Christchurch suburbs such as Oaklands, Woolston, and Kennedys Bush. It is held by National’s Vanessa Weenink, who narrowly won the electorate for the first time in 2023 with a margin of 17,860. National also won the party vote with 32% of the vote, followed by Labour at 27%. The electorate had the highest turnout of any electorate at the 2023 election.

name: Botany
description: Botany covers much of East Auckland, including the suburbs of East Tamaki, Flat Bush, Somerville, and Botany. Since 2020, it has been held by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who easily won re-election with a margin of 24,769 votes. National also won a majority of the party vote at 58%, more than double second-placed Labour’s 22%. The electorate is diverse, boasting a higher proportional Pasifika and Asian population than the rest of New Zealand.

name: Christchurch Central
description: Christchurch Central covers much of inner Christchurch as well as bits from adjoining suburbs such as Sydenham, Beckenham, and Richmond. The electorate has been held by Labour’s Duncan Webb since 2017, who won re-election with 15,553 votes in 2023. National won the party vote in 2023 with 31%, followed by Labour at 28%. In 2011, preliminary results saw a tie on election night, with special votes eventually giving the electorate to National for the first time in its history by just 2 votes.

The last party other than Labour to win the seat was the now-defunct Liberal party in 1922.

name: Coromandel
description: Coromandel covers the Coromandel peninsula, the Hauraki district, and some of the Bay of Plenty, finishing at the edge of Tauranga. Its main population centres include towns such as Thames, Waihi, and Katikati. National’s Scott Simpson has held the electorate since 2011, being re-elected in 2023 with a margin of 24,914 votes. National also won the party vote in 2023 with 43% of the vote, followed by Labour on 20%. The seat has only ever been held by National in the modern era, barring a three year stint where former Green Party leader Jeanette Fitzsimon eked out a 200-vote victory (Labour did not campaign for the electorate vote that year).

name: Dunedin
description: Dunedin covers all but the southern most suburbs of Dunedin city. The electorate is held by Labour’s Rachel Brooking, initially a list MP who was elected in 2023 with a margin of 17,111 votes. Labour also won the party vote with 31%, followed by the Greens on 27%. The electorate skews heavily left; in the two elections with this iteration of the electorate, National has only ever come third to Labour and the Greens in the party vote.

The electorate has been established for this election, however its predecessor East Coast electorate was won by National’s Dana Kirkpatrick by a margin of 17,007 votes. Kirkpatrick will stand for East Cape in 2026. The electorate previously existed between 1978 and 1990.

name: East Coast Bays
description: East Coast Bays covers the north east areas of Auckland city, covering suburbs such as Albany, Pinehill, and Lucas Creek. It has been held by National’s Erica Stanford since 2017, who won re-election in 2023 with a margin of 27,687 votes. National won a majority of the party vote in 2023 with 58%, while Labour was a distant second at 14%. The electorate was one of the few electorates to be won by a third party in the pre-MPP era, with Social Credit holding the seat between 1980 and 1984.

description: Epsom covers central and eastern Auckland, including the suburbs of Remuera, Mount Eden, and Grafton. Act party leader David Seymour has held the seat since 2014, being re-elected in 2023 with a margin of 17,826 votes. National won the party vote in 2023 with 52%, followed by Labour on 15%. Since the seat was created in 1996, it has returned at least one list MP in every election.

name: Glendene
description: Glendene covers west Auckland suburbs, including Avondale, Kelston, and the Te Atatū peninsula. The electorate was founded for the first time in 2026, though its predecessor electorates of Te Atatū and Kelston were only ever held by Labour in the MMP era. In 2023, the now disestablished seat of Kelston was won by Labour's Carmel Sepuloni, who is running in the Glendene seat in 2026.

description: Hamilton East covers Hamilton’s urban eastern half, up to the Waikato River and covers suburbs such as Claudelands, Flagstaff, and Enderly. National’s Ryan Hamilton is the current MP and was first elected in 2023 with a margin of 17,950. National won the party vote in 2023 with 43% of the vote, followed by Labour with 25%. RyanHamilton is the first MP in New Zealand history to have the same last name as his electorate.

description: Hamilton West covers Hamilton’s western half, up until the Waikato River which dives it from Hamilton East. It covers suburbs such as Nawtown, Fitzroy, and Melville. Tama Potaka has been the MP since winning the seat in a 2022 by-election and won re-election with a margin of 17,595. National also won the party vote in 2023 with 41% of the vote, followed by Labour on 26%. The seat is regarded as a bellwether seat, as with the exception of 1993, the seat has always been won by the party which won the plurality of the vote.

It is currently held by National’s Chris Bishop, who won election in 2023 with a margin of 14,772 votes, and who was also the electorate MP from 2017-2020, and being a list MP from 2014. In 2023, the party vote was close, with National winning 34% followed by Labour with 32%. Bishop is only the third-ever MP for Hutt South; his 2017 predecessor Trevor Mallard held it for 21 years before him.

name: Whangārei
description: Surrounded entirely by the Northland electorate, Whangārei forms an alcove around the city of Whangārei and its harbour, and while also stretching south to Waipū and Langs Beach and north to Whangaruru harbour. name: Wigram
description: Wigram covers the south-western suburbs of Christchurch, covering suburbs such as Wigram, Riccarton, Hornby and Sockburn. The seat is currently held by Labour’s Megan Woods, who was first elected in 2011. Woods won in 2023 with 15,590 votes. National won the party vote with 35%, followed by Labour with 29%. The seat is a traditional left-wing stronghold. First formed in 1969, it has only ever been won by a Labour candidate outside the years from 1996 to 2008 that was held by Alliance and Progressive party leader Jim Anderton.

name: Ikaroa-Rāwhiti
description: The Ikaroa-Rāwhiti electorate covers the eastern North Island, including Gisborne, Hawke’s Bay, Waiarapa and  parts of the Hutt Valley in Greater Wellington. The seat is currently held by the Labour Party’s Cushla Tangaere-Manuel, who was the only Labour Party candidate to win a Māori seat in 2023. Tangaere-Manuel won 13,747 votes and 54.79% of the party vote. Since its establishment in 1999, the seat has been a stronghold for the Labour Party. The only time Labour has not controlled the seat was when Labour cabinet minister Meka Whaitiri defected to Te Pāti Māori before being defeated in 2023.

description: Te Tai Tonga is the electorate of the South Island. It covers South Island, Stewart Island, the Chatham Islands, and parts of both Wellington City and the Hutt Valley.
